Use the given values to set up simultaneous linear equations for $f(x) = a + b\sin x$:
$$f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = a + b\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = a + \frac{1}{2}b = 4$$
$$f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = a + b\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = a + b = 3$$

Subtract the first equation from the second:
$$\frac{1}{2}b = -1 \implies b = -2$$
$$a = 3 - (-2) = 5$$
$$a = 5, \quad b = -2$$

Evaluate the outer function at $x = 5$ (in radians):
$$ff(0) = f(5) = 5 - 2\sin(5\text{ radians}) \approx 5 - 2(-0.958924) = 5 + 1.91785 = 6.91785 \approx 6.92 \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

For $g(x) = c + d\sin x$, the range $[-4, 10]$ is determined by the minimum and maximum of the sine function:
$$\text{Maximum: } c + |d| = 10$$
$$\text{Minimum: } c - |d| = -4$$

Solve for the vertical translation $c$ and amplitude $|d|$:
$$2c = 6 \implies c = 3$$
$$|d| = 10 - 3 = 7 \implies d = 7 \quad \text{or} \quad d = -7$$
$$c = 3, \quad d = 7 \quad (\text{or } d = -7)$$
